hypothesis: R257's realized P&L was dominated by repeated strength winners. A low 20-day maximum-single-day-return weakest link should retain quality and industry-relative leadership while avoiding lottery-like one-day spikes. This is distinct from a broad 5-day reversal and does not change R257's internal formula or portfolio constraints.
selection_basis: R258's hard recency gate failed pool capacity, R259's broad 5-day reversal destroyed returns, and R260's soft recency penalty reduced industry concentration but broke validation and recent performance. R261 changes the behavioral mechanism to lottery demand: it penalizes the largest daily jump over 20 days rather than total short-term momentum or repeated Top30 presence. Feasibility read no forward or strategy returns: joint coverage is 99.9211% full, 99.9646% discovery, 99.8797% validation and 99.9122% recent year; the low-lottery component has mean absolute monthly rank correlation 0.102814 with R257, maximum absolute 0.210619; mean absolute correlation with R249 low skew is 0.332760 and maximum absolute is 0.693388; the composite lowers the R257 percentile by 0.173800 on average and is at least 0.10 lower for 39.5726% of observations; every date has at least 246 valid names. Evidence: r261_data_feasibility.json.

factor.formula: quality_low_lottery_min_rank = min(rank_pct(quality_relative_strength_min_rank), rank_pct(-max_ret_20d)) within same-date historical nonfinancial HS300 members; 1 is best

component_definitions.quality_relative_strength_min_rank: R257 composite of the R253 quality weakest link and 20-day stock-relative-to-industry strength
component_definitions.low_max_ret_20d: -(maximum daily close-to-close return over the current and prior 19 trading days), using front-adjusted close

factor.interpretation: A company must remain strong on quality and industry-relative leadership without showing a lottery-like single-day jump.
factor.pit_rule: R257 inherits financial publication/PIT dates and same-date industry-relative strength. max_ret_20d uses front-adjusted closes through date t. Ranks and the minimum use only same-date eligible historical nonfinancial HS300 members.
factor.missing_data_rule: Both components are required; a missing component leaves the composite null.

strategies.common_filter: Current nonfinancial industry snapshot is required; history uses historical HS300 membership. Both strategies require ma60 and non-null quality_low_lottery_min_rank so the candidate and control universe is identical.
strategies.execution: 30-name score limit, at most 10 equal-weight positions, 20-day holding, -20% stop loss, T+1 open execution and 3x costs; candidate also tested at 4x/5x.

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally

segments.stitching: compound two independently run segment curves; skip the first return of each later segment

factor_ic.method: R261 factor month-end rank IC versus T+1 open to T+21 open return within historical nonfinancial HS300 members

gates.D1: full and recent-12-month joint component coverage >=0.99
gates.D2: discovery and validation joint component coverage >=0.99
gates.D3: first valid date is no later than 2023-05-04 and written values exactly match the same-date composite formula with max abs difference <=1e-12
gates.D4: mean absolute monthly R257/low-lottery rank correlation <=0.70, every monthly absolute correlation <=0.80, mean composite reduction versus R257 percentile >=0.05 and at least 20% of observations reduced by >=0.10
gates.D5: mean absolute monthly correlation of the low-lottery component with R249 low skew <=0.70 and every monthly absolute correlation <=0.80
gates.I1: discovery mean R261 rank IC >=0.02 with at least 18 month-end observations
gates.I2: validation mean R261 rank IC >=0.01 with at least 18 month-end observations and the same positive sign
gates.G2: discovery candidate MDD is no worse than control MDD by more than 5pp
gates.G4: full-sample candidate return > 0 and >= control return
gates.G5: full-sample candidate MDD <= 40% in absolute value and no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G6: rolling 1-year positive rate >= 60% and no worse than control by more than 2pp
gates.G7: recent 12-month candidate return > 0 and MDD no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G8: full-sample candidate return at 4x cost is positive
gates.G9: full-sample candidate return at 5x cost is positive
gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full sample
gates.C2: the largest symbol's share of net P&L is <= 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is <= 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is <= 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is <= 45%
gates.C7: the largest single-symbol loss is <= 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All D, I, G and C gates must pass. Any failure means the low-lottery factor is not accepted and cannot be rescued by changing the 20-day window, component weights, rank direction, holding period, stop loss, universe, costs or gates after seeing results.
known_limitations: This is a result-driven follow-up to R257/R258/R259/R260 and not independent confirmation.
Maximum daily return is outlier-sensitive and moderately related to R249 low skew.
The minimum of two percentile ranks can be sparse and sensitive to ties.
R253 and industry-relative strength were researched in overlapping samples, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
The nonfinancial industry snapshot is current rather than historical PIT.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments and segment boundaries can reset open positions.
Passing these gates would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
